claims.text: Faculty evaluations are frequently criticized for being subjective, inconsistent, and shaped by institutional cultures.
Structural and resource imbalances between public and private institutions exacerbate subjectivity and inconsistency in faculty evaluations.
AI technology can be structured into equity-driven frameworks to evaluate faculty contributions across teaching, research, and service.

evidence.description: The authors note that faculty evaluations are frequently criticized for being subjective, inconsistent, and shaped by institutional cultures.
The authors state that structural and resource imbalances between public and private institutions exacerbate issues of subjectivity and inconsistency.
The chapter outlines theoretical frameworks and practical examples using AI technology to evaluate faculty contributions across teaching, research, and service.

methodologies.name: Equity-Driven AI Faculty Evaluation Framework
methodologies.description: A conceptual framework leveraging AI technology to assess faculty performance across teaching, research, and service while addressing ethical deployment and institutional disparities.
